subject: SummitBridge SI onboarding: gating issues & SIEM compatibility blockers
messages:
From: SummitBridge Integrations <integrations@summitbridge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: SIEM connector: observed schema mismatch in marketplace bundle

Hi Jordan / Monica,

Thanks again for the onboarding call last week. We're spinning up the marketplace bundle for SummitBridge and hit two blockers that are preventing the SI from completing the entitlement verification:

1) The SIEM connector uses a nested event envelope (source->events[]) that doesn't match the marketplace's ingestor expectation (flat event per message). Transforming on our side adds unacceptable latency for real-time alerts.
2) The current marketplace listing validation rejects bundles that include an "entitlements.json" with nested permission objects—our packaging tool outputs that file by default.

I've attached the connector spec and a screenshot of the marketplace validation error. Can Redwood advise if there's a recommended adapter pattern or whether the marketplace can accept our nested envelope in a feature-flagged listing?

Attachments: summitbridge-siem-spec.pdf (PDF, 345KB), marketplace-gating-screenshot.png (PNG, 87KB)

Appreciate any quick pointers—these two items are gating our go-live next sprint.

Best,
Alex Chen
Integrations Lead, SummitBridge
integrations@summitbridge.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: SummitBridge Integrations <integrations@summitbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 15:44:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SIEM connector: observed schema mismatch in marketplace bundle

Alex —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Short answers up front: we can support both asks, but each has tradeoffs and product/ops coordination required. High-level plan below, followed by specific asks from Product/SI/Marketplace teams.

Plan (short):
- Short-term workaround: Redwood can publish a compatibility shim on behalf of SummitBridge that flattens the envelope at the ingestion edge (adds ~15ms median per event) to unblock listing. This requires a support ticket + Marketplace sign-off.
- Medium-term: engineering change to the marketplace ingestor to accept an envelope mode behind a listing-level feature flag. That work touches entitlements validation and the ingestion schema contract.

Product asks for the engineering intake:
- Monica / Ben: can you triage whether the marketplace validation can be updated to accept an "envelope_mode" schema option for partner bundles? If yes, what's the estimated effort (story points) and cross-team owners?
- SummitBridge: can you produce a minimal example (1-2 sample events) that demonstrates the nested envelope semantics and the expected downstream mapping? The spec you sent is helpful but a tiny payload will accelerate this.

Operational asks:
- If we publish a shim, Legal will need to approve the alteration to the published bundle and the support SLA implications. Alex — please loop in your legal contact so we can get a quick review.
- For the shim publish, we need a short maintenance window (non-peak) for Canary verification; ops will schedule after we confirm timing.

I'll defer to Monica/Ben for triage and timelines. I can own the partner comms.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SIEM connector: observed schema mismatch in marketplace bundle

Thanks Jordan—looping in engineering ops and marketplace infra leads by mention in Jira (RED-3419). Quick operational notes from triage:

- Marketplace validation: the entitlement schema validator is relatively small; adding an "envelope_mode" option should be a 3–5 day task (backend + validation tests) and a short UI tweak to allow selection during bundle upload. Owner: Marketplace Infra (TBD), impact: low.
- Ingest shim: we can publish a partner-side compatibility shim, but it requires an explicit exception in our listing policy so Marketplace Legal signs off. The shim will run in the ingestion path and add ~10–20ms p95 for large event spikes (we measured similar shims for other partners). Ops prefers the feature-flag update to avoid ongoing shim maintenance.

Next steps / asks:
1) Alex — please add a 2–3 event sample payload to the Doc (use the Google Doc link Jordan included).
2) Ben — can you estimate SRE effort for the ingestion shim rollout (smoke test + canary window)?
3) Jordan — I'll kick off RED-3419 and tag Marketplace Infra and Legal for formal sign-off.

Monica
Director, Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 16:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SIEM connector: observed schema mismatch in marketplace bundle

Jordan / Monica — quick estimate from SRE:

- Ingest shim rollout: 2 engineers x 3 days + 1 day for canary validation = roughly 7 engineer-days (including runbook updates). We'll need a short scheduled window (~30 minutes) in the evening pacific to run the canary. No infra changes required beyond the shim deployment.
- Monitoring: we will add two additional metrics (shim_latency_ms and shim_dropped_events) and a temporary dashboard.

Operational caveats: if SummitBridge's event sizes or burst patterns exceed our baseline, we may need autoscaling adjustments; that adds ~2 days for SRE + infra tickets. Recommend SummitBridge provide a representative 24-hour event trace if possible.

I'll schedule the canary as soon as we have legal sign-off and SummitBridge example payloads.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
